subject: Re: BrightCore - degraded latency & errors after model upgrade
messages:
From: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@brightcore.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ward <tom.ward@brightcore.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency spike + increased generation errors since last night’s upgrade

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a ~2.5x P95 latency increase and a higher rate of hallucinated entity insertions in our customer-facing summarization flow after the model upgrade that your team rolled last night (redwood-open-7B-quant-v2). Volume hasn’t changed on our side — the only change was the model version you switched us to.

Attached is a short sample of degraded outputs and our internal latency CSV (brightcore_latency_report_20261031.csv). This is blocking an ongoing pilot and our execs are asking for immediate remediation.

Can you confirm whether BrightCore can be reverted to the previous serving profile while you investigate? We need a rollback or mitigation plan within 4 hours if possible.

Thanks,
Elena Ortiz
Head of ML Platforms | BrightCore Analytics
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@brightcore.ai>, Tom Ward <tom.ward@brightcore.ai>

Subject: Re: Latency spike + increased generation errors since last night’s upgrade

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts.

We are escalating this immediately. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS) and Neha (Infra/Runtime) to triage. Initial ask: we’ll schedule a short incident call in 20 minutes. If rollback is the safest immediate step we will coordinate a controlled revert to the previous quant profile (redwood-open-7B-quant-v1).

Marissa — please run link to the incident playbook and pull the metrics we need (P50/P95/P99, error rate by tenant, and the active quant profile). Neha — please capture the node-level queue/backpressure metrics and whether any kernel fallbacks were triggered after the upgrade.

Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Running now. Early read: BrightCore is pinned to the new quant-v2 profile on their dedicated pool. P95 jumped from ~420ms to ~1.05s; error rate (bad JSON/failed parse) increased from 0.6% to 3.8% after the deploy window (00:15–00:24 UTC).

I’ve attached the customer CSV from Elena to our incident ticket and added a short notes doc in the Drive link. Also confirming: BrightCore is in our Dedicated (reserved) fleet in us-east-1, single-region.

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike + increased generation errors since last night’s upgrade

On Sat, Oct 31, 2026 at 09:02 AM marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Early read: BrightCore is pinned to the new quant-v2 profile...

Quick technical summary from runtime: the quant-v2 profile includes a more aggressive per-layer int8 packing and a small change to KV cache formatting intended to reduce memory. While CPU offload and reduced memory look good in benchmarks, we’re seeing degraded kernel throughput for sequence lengths common to BrightCore’s workload (~420 tokens). Evidence: increased kernel swaps and more frequent kernel fallback to slower paths when cache hits are lower; this explains the P95 jump. We also flagged a regression in the logits-sanitizer that allowed malformed token sequences in edge cases — that’s driving the small but notable rise in parsing errors.

Immediate mitigation options (pros/cons):
- Rollback to quant-v1 (safe, immediate latency improvement, requires ~10–15min maintenance window on their pool).
- Apply an emergency config change: disable the new per-layer packing for BrightCore only (fast, targeted; risk: unknown perf impact on memory).
- Throttle aggressively and enable a temporary prefix cache bypass (will reduce error rate but hurts throughput).

I recommend rollback for BrightCore and a hotfix for the logits sanitizer. We should also draft an exec update for both Redwood and BrightCore stakeholders.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Eng, Runtime & Inference | Redwood Inference
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@brightcore.ai>, Tom Ward <tom.ward@brightcore.ai>

Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency spike + increased generation errors since last night’s upgrade

Elena / Tom — we will perform a controlled rollback of BrightCore’s dedicated pool to redwood-open-7B-quant-v1 at 10:30 PST (10:30 UTC-8). This will be announced with a 15-minute maintenance notice to your engineers.

High-level actions we are taking now:
- Neha’s infra team will revert the quant profile and monitor kernels for 30 minutes post-rollback.
- Marissa will coordinate customer comms and exec touchpoint. I’m preparing a short summary for your CTO and our VP of Product.
- We are creating a hotfix ticket for the logits sanitizer regression and will prioritise validation in the next deploy window.

Expect a final confirmation within 45 minutes. Our goal is to restore pre-upgrade latency and error rates, and then run a postmortem to prevent recurrence.

— Stephanie
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ortiz <e.ortiz@brightcore.ai>, Tom Ward <tom.ward@brightcore.ai>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: BrightCore rollback complete — performance restored; exec summary attached

Hi Elena and Tom —

Update: We completed the rollback to redwood-open-7B-quant-v1 on BrightCore’s dedicated pool at 16:55 UTC on 2026-11-02. P95 returned to ~430ms within 12 minutes, and the parsing error rate dropped back to 0.7%. The attached action plan (redwood_action_plan_v1.pdf) outlines next steps: a hotfix for the logits sanitizer, a canary of a revised quant-v2.1 with less aggressive packing, and an extended validation gate for dedicated customers.

What we did immediately:
- Rolled the quant profile back on the tenant-specific config (no tenant migration required).
- Ran a 30-minute watch on kernel fallbacks and memory metrics; no anomalies post-rollback.
- Flagged the quant packing change and disabled it for canary customers pending further tuning.

Next steps we propose with timelines:
1) Hotfix for logits sanitizer — targeted test suite by Wed 2026-11-04.
2) Quant-v2.1 canary (less aggressive packing) — internal canary next week, customer canaries after validation.
3) Joint postmortem with BrightCore — proposal to schedule on 2026-11-05.

I’ll sync with your team to schedule the postmortem and share the internal RCA once complete. Please let me know if you need an executive-level note for your board.

Thanks for your patience — we’ll follow up with the RCA and timelines.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
